title: just-deliver catalog component
description: What a workload asks for by name (for example 'database'): one contract, and an implementation per platform and environment type. Expressions (${...}) are kept as raw strings by the loader and evaluated later. Unique by name across shared resources, components and runtimes.

name.description: Value teams write as 'type' in a workload requirement; same pattern as the workload schema's type.

description.description: What the component gives a team.

exports.description: The contract: the only valid names in ${resource.<id>.<name>}. Every class of every implementation exports exactly these (checked by the resolver).

x-jd.message: uses belongs in each platform entry of implementations, since what a component uses depends on how it is built; a catalog written for an older jd has it here, so move it (see catalog/components/database.yaml).

implementations.description: Platform (declared in the Catalog file) -> what the component is on it. An environment uses its platform's entry, with no fallback: a component without one is not offered on that platform.

uses.description: The shared resources of this platform its parts may read as ${<name>.<export>} (checked by the resolver).

types.description: Environment type (declared in the Catalog file) or 'default' -> implementation. An environment uses its type's implementation, else 'default'; every implementation declares the same classes (checked by the resolver).

environment.description: The nodes deployed once per environment that offers the component, and their exports; its class parts read them as ${<component>.<export>}.

classes.description: Class (what a workload may request with 'class') -> the nodes each requiring workload gets and its exports.

x-jd.message: not a field of a platform entry (uses, types); a catalog written for an older jd keys implementations by environment type, so put them under a platform's types (see catalog/components/database.yaml).
